Entries.Text: EDGE files are only used by Sekiro.
Edit the grapple points, hangable ledges and huggable walls of a collision. Each collision's EDGE file is in its map's edgebhd, and its points are relative to the collision part.
Whether the EDGE points are drawn in the viewport.
EDGE points are hidden, so edits won't show in the viewport.
Turn on the EDGE Points filter, which draws the points on collision and asset parts.
The colours the points are drawn in, by type, and their sizes. The entry selected below is drawn larger, in the selected colour and over the geometry.
A point the grappling hook can reach.
The smaller sphere a grapple pulls the player towards, and the line joining it to its grapple point.
A segment of a ledge that can be hung from.
A segment of a wall that can be hugged.
The entry selected in this tool.
The handle under the cursor while editing in the viewport. Used the next time the cursor moves onto a handle.
The radius of the grapple point spheres, in metres. Pull points are drawn at 60% of it.
The radius of the ledge and wall cylinders, in metres. Pull lines are drawn at 40% of it.
The collision part whose EDGE file is edited: the last one whose point was clicked while editing in the viewport, or the last collision part selected in the viewport or the map's contents.
Turn on Edit in Viewport and click a displayed EDGE point, or select one collision part, to edit its EDGE file.
Click a displayed EDGE point or ledge in the viewport to edit its collision's file.
{0} has no EDGE files, or they couldn't be read.
{0} has no EDGE file. Create an empty one here, or add a grapple point or draw a ledge on it in the viewport, which creates it.
Add an empty EDGE file for this collision to the map's edgebhd, with the collision's number as its ID (as every game file has).
Pick and move the EDGE points of any displayed collision in the viewport.
While on, clicks in the viewport pick the EDGE points of every displayed collision instead of selecting parts. Turn it off to select parts again. It also stops while this tool isn't shown.
What a click in the viewport does.

Click any displayed point to pick it: its collision becomes the one edited here, and the gizmo moves the point freely. Drag a point to slide it over its collision under the cursor. A chain's shared point moves every segment that meets there; a grapple's direction point moves with it. Click a ledge or wall to select its entry.

Click a collision to add a grapple point there, with its direction point 4 cm above it and no pull point, as the game's map grapples are. It goes to the collision under the cursor, which gets an EDGE file if it has none.

Click points on the collision to lay down a ledge, one segment per click. Start on a ledge's end to continue it; end on another ledge's opposite end to join the two. New ledges get the next free chain ID and Variation 0.

Click points on the collision to lay down a huggable wall, one segment per click. Start on a wall's end to continue it; end on another wall's opposite end to join the two. New walls get the next free chain ID and Variation 1.
Click a collision to start a chain, or a chain's end to continue it.
Click where the first segment ends.
Click to add a segment, or on the opposite end of another chain of this type to join them. Escape or Enter stops.
The chain being drawn changed (e.g. by an undo), so drawing stopped.
Stop drawing. The segments placed so far stay.
Nothing to place on under the cursor. Points go on shown collision parts whose triangles are loaded (load the map with collision), or on displayed EDGE points.
EDGE points are hidden, so there is nothing to pick. Display them above.
This collision's triangles aren't loaded, so a dragged point stays at the distance it was picked at. Load the map with collision to drag over it.
Under the cursor: segment of entry {0} of {1}
The entries of the EDGE file, in file order. Ledges and walls are segments; segments with the same chain ID meet end to end. Double-click an entry to frame it in the viewport.
List the entries under their chains (by type and chain ID) and the grapple points together, rather than in file order. The selected entry's chain opens by itself.
The fields of the selected entry. A change is applied when you leave the input, and can be undone.
Grapple: a point the grappling hook can reach. Hang: a ledge that can be hung from. Hug: a wall that can be hugged.
The start of the segment, relative to the collision part.
The end of the segment, relative to the collision part. The next segment of the chain usually starts here.
The grapple point, relative to the collision part.
A second point a few centimetres from the position (3.5 cm in the middle of the game's files), giving the grapple point a direction.
The point the player is pulled towards, relative to the collision part. Zero when the grapple point has none.
1 when the grapple point has a pull point, 0 when it doesn't (always so in the game's files).
The chain the segment belongs to. Segments of a chain share this and meet end to end (Unk30).
Unk30. A number from 1 upward, as on ledges and walls, where it is the chain ID.
For grapple points, a relative ID in WireVariationParam. Ledges use 0 or 1, walls 0 to 3 or 10.
Load the params to see the WireVariationParam row.
Changes to the entries of the file. Each can be undone.
Insert a copy of the selected entry after it.
Remove the selected entry from the file.
Split the selected ledge or wall segment in two at its middle, joined by a new chain point.
Remove every segment of the selected segment's chain (same type and chain ID).

Remove the point picked in the viewport. A grapple point removes its entry, a pull point is taken off its grapple, a chain's end shortens it by a segment, and a point inside a chain joins its two segments into one.
Give the selected grapple a pull point 0.5 m above it and set Has Pull Point, as object EDGE files do. None of the game's map grapples have one.
Take the selected grapple's pull point away and clear Has Pull Point.

Things in this file that look like mistakes. They are warnings: the game's own files have a few (2 degenerate segments and 31 loops left open by under 1 cm, of 689 map files). Click one to select its entry, double-click to frame it.
Fix every issue listed, as one action.
A ledge or wall segment whose start and end are the same point.
An entry exactly the same as an earlier one.
Entry {0}: ledge or wall with a pull point
Only grapple points use a pull point or Has Pull Point; no ledge or wall in the game has one.
Clear the pull point and Has Pull Point.
Entry {0}: Has Pull Point doesn't match the pull point
In every game file, Has Pull Point is 1 when a grapple has a pull point and 0 when it doesn't.
Set Has Pull Point from whether the grapple has a pull point.
The grapple's direction point is the grapple point itself. In the game's files it is a few centimetres above it.
Put the direction point 4 cm above the grapple point.
Entry {0}: chain end {1} mm from a start it doesn't meet

A chain's end that almost meets another start of the same chain (within 5 cm). The game reuses chain IDs for separate pieces, but never leaves them this close, apart from a few loops open by under 1 cm.
Move the end onto the start, joining them.
Edits are written to the map's edgebhd when the map is saved.
